text:
Drew O'Connor has been through a lot of losing in Vancouver this fall, and The Province framed his month as the "crushing weight of rebuild" starting to ease. His goal in the 6-3 win at Vegas was his third of the season, and only his second point in 10 games.

His finishing has run cold: three goals on 4.4 expected, and the Canucks have scored 3.8 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. That usually swings back. His chance rate is down too, though, from 0.92 expected goals per 60 last season to 0.71, and his ice time over the last 10 games has dropped almost three minutes, with two nights near nine minutes.

The tools are obvious. He's 6'4" with 95th-percentile top speed, and Vancouver's expected-goal share is 5 points better with him than without him, even if it's only 42.8% overall. Evolving-Hockey notes his teammates rank in the bottom 4% by impact, which drags his raw numbers down. Reporter Daniel Wagner wrote that Brendan Gallagher had been finding his stride alongside O'Connor and Max Sasson.
